title: Minnesota's 3rd Congressional District Election, 2026
description: Minnesota's 3rd Congressional District covers the western suburbs of the Twin Cities, including Bloomington, Eden Prairie, Edina, Maple Grove, Minnetonka, Plymouth, Brooklyn Park, Coon Rapids, and Wayzata. Incumbent Democrat Kelly Morrison, first elected in 2024 with 58.4% of the vote, is seeking a second term in a district that was held by Republicans for decades before Democrat Dean Phillips flipped it in 2018. The Republican primary field features small business owner Tyler Bass and retired attorney Quentin Wittrock, with the primary scheduled for August 11, 2026. The Cook Political Report rates the general election as 'Solid D,' reflecting the district's recent leftward shift in demographic and voting patterns.
polling_note: No public opinion polls for this specific race were found as of mid-2026. The race is rated 'Solid D' by Cook Political Report, 'Solid D' by Inside Elections, and 'Safe D' by Sabato's Crystal Ball.

candidates.name: Kelly Morrison
candidates.summary: Kelly Morrison is an obstetrician-gynecologist who has served as the U.S. Representative for Minnesota's 3rd Congressional District since January 2025. A former Minnesota state senator and state representative, she was first elected to Congress in 2024 after the retirement of Rep. Dean Phillips. She is the only OB-GYN in Congress and has focused on reproductive rights, healthcare access, and veterans' issues.

Bass has not previously held elected office.

forecast.rationale: No district-specific polling exists, which tempers confidence, but the non-polling evidence is decisively favorable for Democrats. Incumbent Kelly Morrison won the seat in 2024 with 58.4% of the vote in a district that has shifted leftward after decades of Republican control prior to 2018. Cook Political Report rates the race 'Solid D,' Inside Elections rates it 'Solid D,' and Sabato's Crystal Ball rates it 'Safe D.' The Republican primary (August 11, 2026) features two non-incumbent, first-time candidates (Tyler Bass and Quentin Wittrock) with no prior elected office, suggesting a weak general-election challenge. Given Morrison's strong 2024 margin (roughly 17 points), the district's continued leftward trend, and the absence of any polling suggesting competitiveness, Democrats hold an overwhelming advantage. The safe_d rating reflects a ~95%+ win probability consistent with the consensus of independent election analysts.
